items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch.

ctx.x: Did you say P-Ron would play for a special class of people though, huh?

Yeah, he played for the better class of people, see. He played for the doctors and the lawyers and people up here on St. Charles Street, people back in the place and all that kind of people, the higher class of people, see. And they liked that sweet music and slow and waltzes a lot of things, you know, something like that. Well, the average band around here didn't play that, see. Like John Robeshoe and P-Ron. And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch. Now they played all that kind of…
He had a good band. I had a good band.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Oh, him and Peter Bocard then used to play together on those parades... But Peter Bocard then was playing, that was too much for me. I was playing strictly about music... So I stayed out of that.

ctx.x: What age were you then when you started clarinet?

I was around, I was around 17 years old. 16 or 17 years old when I started playing clarinet. And then various bands used to come from here over there. And when they'd come, I'd bring my clarinet. You'd swear I was going to work out. Bring my clarinet. Peter go in. This is big. They have my clarinet with me. I'd get in there and I'd beg them to let me play with them. Sometime they'd turn me down and sometime they'd let me play. But after you let me play once, then they wouldn't have no trouble. I wouldn't have no…
Who were some of those guys?
